name: HQNP (high quality normie pheno)

card.summary: A looksmax.org label for a conventionally attractive woman with a mainstream, non-exotic phenotype, used as a reference point for what community members consider a broadly appealing look.
card.note: Community slang with no formal definition; usage varies by poster.

quick.overview:
HQNP stands for high quality normie pheno(type). On looksmax.org it describes a woman whose looks are polished and conventionally attractive without being unusual, exotic or extreme.

For people working on their own looks, the term works as a shared yardstick: members compare what they consider a typical high-end mainstream look and discuss which traits create it, such as skin, grooming and proportion. It is a vocabulary item, not a method or product.
quick.how: Members use the label in thread titles and rating posts, for example asking whether a photographed woman looks HQNP, or sharing examples they consider ideal. Some threads treat it as a target to discuss in dating and approaching contexts. There is no routine to follow.
quick.risks: The term is subjective and tied to forum culture, where it sits alongside rating scales and other labels. Photos posted under it are opinions of strangers. No health risk arises from the term itself.

lead: HQNP, short for high quality normie phenotype, is a label used on looksmax.org for a conventionally attractive woman with a mainstream rather than exotic appearance [1][2]. It combines a quality grade (high quality) with a type (normie, meaning an ordinary-looking, mainstream phenotype), and it is applied to photos of women, to online personalities and sometimes to lifestyle traits [2][7].

Members use it as a reference point. Thread titles ask whether a given person looks HQNP, collect examples of an ideal HQNP look, name specific people as definitions of it, request ratings, and compare it against other phenotype labels [3][4][8][11]. A guide-style thread discusses how to find HQNP women, and another debates whether the category exists at all [5][6]. The term sits alongside the wider vocabulary of the forums, which Wikipedia describes as including the PSL scale, with its tiers of normie, Chadlite and Chad, and terms such as Stacy [13].

How it helps someone's own looks is indirect: the label gives members a shared description of a widely appealing look, and discussions around it compare traits such as skin, hair, styling and grooming. Its meaning is set by usage, with no published definition. Attractiveness research uses different vocabulary, studying features such as averageness, symmetry, skin condition and sexual dimorphism [14].

angle.text: People use the term as vocabulary for discussing what a broadly appealing look consists of. It describes a type of appearance; it does not itself change anyone's looks.

paras: The label combines a quality grade (high quality) with a phenotype type (normie, meaning mainstream) [1][2]. Posters apply it to photos of women and to online personalities, and sometimes to personality or lifestyle traits, as in a thread claiming women who own cats are very HQNP [7]. A 2022 thread titled 'does she look hqnp' asks members to judge a photograph against the type [2].

Wikipedia's article on looksmaxxing explains that the culture grew out of 2010s message boards and is organised around terms such as normie and Chad, tiers on the PSL scale, a roughly one-to-eight facial rating system whose upper tiers include Chadlite, Chad and giga Chad [13]. HQNP is a forum-specific coinage layered on top of this vocabulary and is not defined in that article [13].

The earliest HQNP threads in the sources date from 2021, among them a guide-style thread on how to scout for HQNP women [5], with further threads through 2022, 2023 and 2025 [1][2][3][4][6]. The label appears to have stayed within looksmax.org and similar forums; no mainstream coverage using the term was found.

Wikipedia describes the broader looksmaxxing scene as having moved from incel-era forums to TikTok, Kick and other platforms in the early to mid 2020s, with coverage from outlets including The Guardian, The New York Times and The New Yorker [13]. HQNP itself is not named in that coverage.

Threads include rating requests, 'does she look HQNP' questions, praise threads, questions about how to interact with HQNP women, and debates about whether HQNP women are rare, plentiful or mythical [1][3][4][6][8][9]. Contributors disagree about boundaries. Some threads contrast it with posts they consider heavily styled or cosmetic [9]. Other threads pair it with ethnicity or region in collections of photos, such as a thread collecting what its title calls HQNP Arab girls [12].

No published research uses the term HQNP. Attractiveness studies examine measurable features. Wikipedia's facial attractiveness article summarises findings that composite or averaged faces are often rated as more attractive, that facial symmetry has been linked in some studies to preferences, that cross-cultural raters show considerable agreement on attractiveness, and that skin colour and condition influence ratings [14]. These studies do not map onto the forum's categories.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, HQNP is used both as a descriptive label and as a topic of argument about whether the type is attainable or common [1][6].

claims.claim: HQNP is an identifiable female look
claims.believers: Posters share examples and name individuals as definitions of the type, treating it as recognisable at a glance [3][4].
claims.experts: No published research uses this term; attractiveness studies examine averageness, symmetry and skin without this label.

claims.claim: HQNP women are rare or do not exist
claims.believers: At least one thread argues the category is a myth, while others treat it as a defined target [5][6].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined this forum category.

claims.claim: HQNP is a good example of what a mainstream attractive woman looks like
claims.believers: Posters share examples and name individuals as definitions, praising them as ideal HQNP [3][4].
claims.experts: Attractiveness researchers study averageness, symmetry and skin condition rather than forum categories [14].

claims.claim: HQNP is separate from heavily styled or cosmetic looks
claims.believers: A thread titled with a complaint about what members post contrasts HQNP preference with posts of heavily styled women [9].
claims.experts: No studies have compared these categories; the cosmetic literature does not use them.

claims.claim: Traits beyond looks, such as lifestyle, can count as HQNP
claims.believers: A 2022 thread argues women who own cats are very HQNP [7].
claims.experts: No published research ties pet ownership to perceived attractiveness in this sense.
